labels.label: T-loc-ealpha-cauchy/1-cauchy-axis-kept
labels.notes: massive_globallyHyperbolic_isCauchySurface : (massive α).GloballyHyperbolic ∧ (massive α).IsCauchySurface {p | p.1 = 0}, under [Fact (0 < α)] only. Both predicates are the ladder's own: Causality.GloballyHyperbolic (Causal/Properties.lean:144, ladder id globally_hyperbolic) and Causality.IsCauchySurface = IsCauchySurfaceOn ⊤ (Causal/Cauchy.lean:70-74, DEC-14: every inextensible causal curve meets S in exactly one point). Massive α = ℝ × Cone α keeps the apex as points; massive α = staticCausality (Cone α). Every slice (massive_isCauchySurface_slice) via isCauchyTimeFunction_sub_const and Geroch (ii)⇒(iii). Lean ≥ the target and ≥ Hörmann: DEC-14 tests every inextensible causal curve, timelike ones included, so a DEC-14 Cauchy surface is one in Hörmann's sense (hormann2015conical.txt:271-277); the curve-notion gap (ETT 1-Lipschitz graphs vs L∞/C¹) is disclosed in the checklist. α range: the only hypothesis on α is Fact (0 < α), so every total angle α > 0 (Hörmann: 0 < α_H < 1, α = 2π α_H) holds as claimed. The 3+1 reading E_α × ℝ_z is covered with the same strength (cosmicString_globallyHyperbolic_isCauchySurface, every t₀), so the label is certified under either reading of 'E_α × ℝ'.

labels.label: T-loc-ealpha-cauchy/2-axis-removed
labels.notes: not_isCauchySurfaceOn_regOpens_slice : ¬ (massive α).IsCauchySurfaceOn (regOpens α) ({p | p.1 = 0} ∩ regPart α). 'Axis removed' is genuinely the open set: regOpens α = staticCausality.offOpens isClosed_singleton = {p | p.2 ∉ {apex}}, coe_regOpens = regPart α by rfl, and staticLe U is defined by 1-Lipschitz graphs lying in U (Causal/Static.lean:305), so ≤_reg and Inextensible (regOpens α) use reg's own curves (kb/0001). Not vacuous: a negated IsCauchySurfaceOn can only be proved by exhibiting an inextensible curve of reg (IsCauchySurfaceOn ∅ S is vacuously true), and the witness massive_infall 0 is proved inextensible in reg over Iio 0, chronal on every segment (speed 1/2), radius −τ/2 > 0 (in reg), first coordinate τ < 0 (misses {t = 0}); since it is timelike, the slice also fails Hörmann's timelike notion. Stronger forms proved: any subset of any slice; no S at all (not_exists_isCauchySurfaceOn_regOpens); not GloballyHyperbolicOn (diamond from (−2, r 1) to (2, r 1) not closed in reg). 3+1 versions on stringOffAxis α likewise. See minor finding on the wording 'exactly Ellis–Schmidt's claim' for the no-Cauchy-surface extra.

labels.label: T-loc-ealpha-cauchy/3-past-through-axis
labels.notes: massive_Jminus_axis_inter_slice t₀ : J⁻((t₀, apex)) ∩ {t = 0} = {p | p.1 = 0 ∧ rad p.2 ≤ t₀}: the closed disc of radius t₀ about the axis, the right set (empty for t₀ < 0, the axis point for t₀ = 0), from J⁻(x) ∩ {t = t₁} = {t₁} ×ˢ closedBall x.2 (x.1 − t₁) (static le_top_iff: dist ≤ Δt) and rad = dist apex. Null cone (J⁻ \ I⁻) ∩ {t = 0} = {rad = t₀}. Jminus ⊤ {x} is the library's J⁻. The reading 'x on the axis' is disclosed, and the formula for every x plus the decomposition J⁻(x) = J⁻_reg(x) ∪ ⋃_{ξ ∈ J⁻(x) ∩ axis} J⁻(ξ) close every other reading. 3+1: r² + (z − z₀)² ≤ t₀² with 0 ≤ t₀, correct for the L² product (the length metric of dr² + r²dθ² + dz²). The open question on when the axis part of the decomposition is needed is hedged, not claimed.

findings.what: The docstring for label 4 says 'every ladder property for cosmicString α (cosmicString_*)'. programme/ladder.toml has 13 causality-sort properties; causally_plain (Causal.Causality.CausallyPlain) is not instantiated for cosmicString α (nor for massive α, which the REPORT discloses). The overclaim concerns an extra beyond the target's provides list, not the provides itself.

findings.what: 'reg(E_α) admits NO Cauchy surface whatsoever …, which is exactly Ellis–Schmidt's claim' overstates. A DEC-14 Cauchy surface must be met once by every inextensible CAUSAL curve, so 'no DEC-14 Cauchy surface' is weaker than Ellis–Schmidt's classical 'no Cauchy surface' (tested on timelike curves only), and the three-curve proof of not_exists_isCauchySurfaceOn uses null rays (speed 1), so it does not give the timelike form. The REPORT's question entry does say the Lean is the ETT reading, so this is a wording issue in a finding that would go to the author, not a false finding. The target's own slice assertion is unaffected: its witness massive_infall is chronal.
findings.fix: Reword to 'Ellis–Schmidt's claim in ETT's causal-curve reading (DEC-14)'. Optionally redo the three-curve argument with speed-1/2 rays to cover the timelike form.
